info.name: Cassini Live
info.summary: Private live captions for Nextcloud Talk, recognised on your own server. Early release.
info.description:
Live captions for Talk calls, recognised on your own server and shown in a transcript panel beside the call. Audio and captions stay on your infrastructure: no account, API key, GPU, recording or saved transcript.
## An early release
Cassini Live is a work in progress, and it is not yet a native part of Talk. Talk connects its **Show captions** button to one fixed app, Nextcloud's own Live Transcription, and no other app can take that place. So Cassini Live works beside Talk:
- **In the browser**, it adds its own transcript panel to the Talk page. Each person opens it from a bookmark, and captions start from there, not from Talk's button. - **On the server**, it listens to the call through Talk's High-performance backend, recognises the speech and delivers the captions.
Expect rough edges. Please read the [known limitations](https://github.com/codemyriad/cassini-live/blob/main/docs/known-limitations.md) before you install. Feedback is welcome and decides what we fix first: tell us what works and what doesn't in [GitHub issues](https://github.com/codemyriad/cassini-live/issues).
## What you get
- **Live captions with names.** Each speaker's words appear under their Talk name, including your own. - **A transcript panel in the call sidebar.** Scroll back through the call; people who join late see what was said before they arrived. Nothing is saved once the call's captions end. - **Seven languages on a CPU.** Whistle, bundled, recognises English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch and Polish, with automatic language detection. - **More accurate engines on request.** Administrators can switch the server to Nemotron English (NVIDIA Open Model License) or Nemotron Multilingual (OpenMDW-1.1). Their models are downloaded from dist.gocassini.com when chosen, not shipped in the image. - **Safe under load.** Cassini Live needs enforced CPU, memory and process limits, and captions fewer speakers rather than everyone late when the server can't keep up.
## Turning captions on
Each person adds the transcript panel to their browser once, as a bookmark, from the **Cassini Live** page in Nextcloud's app menu. In a Talk call, a click on the bookmark opens the panel and starts captions for that person. This needs a Nextcloud login: guests can't start captions or open the panel.
Nextcloud's Live Transcription app can stay installed; Talk's **Show captions** button keeps driving it.
## Requirements
- Nextcloud 33 to 35 with Talk's High-performance backend, AppAPI and a deploy daemon. - The HPB internal secret, entered once after installation: the **Cassini Live** page in the app menu shows administrators what is left to set up and links to the settings page. Its URL is discovered from Talk. - Linux with cgroup v2, and CPU, memory and PID limits set on the container (`nc_app_cassini_live`) after installation: until then Cassini Live loads no engine. The [installation guide](https://github.com/codemyriad/cassini-live/blob/main/docs/install.md) has the commands. Whistle needs about 2 GiB of container memory; Nemotron 2.25-3 GiB, and twice that on the host.
## Related
Cassini Live is a companion to [Cassini](https://apps.nextcloud.com/apps/gocassini), which records and transcribes Talk meetings.

variable.name: CASSINI_TALK_SIGNALING_INTERNAL_SECRET
variable.description: The signalling server's [clients] internalsecret, not the shared secret in Talk settings. On AIO: docker exec nextcloud-aio-talk printenv INTERNAL_SECRET. Alternatively, leave this empty and enter it on the Cassini Live settings page after installation.

variable.name: CASSINI_TALK_HPB_URL
variable.description: Leave empty to discover from Talk. Override only when the container needs a different address. Can also be set on the Cassini Live settings page.

variable.name: CASSINI_LIVE_DEBUG_VIDEO
variable.description: Set to 1 to show aggregate server metrics as a video participant in the first captioned room. Visible to everyone there. One feed per server, 1 fps; stops under resource pressure. Default off. The admin-only diagnostics page shows the same without this option.
